statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 10% while Stress is extreme at 80%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. NQ trades at 29,471.00, up 0.08%, inside an overnight band of 29,364.00 to 29,508.25 that has not extended in either direction this hour. The marginal high printed in the previous hour was rejected and has not been retested, and the low was faded earlier, so both extremes have produced retracements rather than the persistent no-pullback structure that defines tail conditions. VIX unchanged at 16.46 confirms no tail repricing in options, and the 10-year at 4.84% and 2-year at 4.43% are both marginally lower on the day, so the yield impulse that drove three consecutive lower closes has paused. Stress stays extreme because Brent above $100, a 10-year near its highest since late 2023 and market-implied odds close to 60% for a rate increase on 16 September make the environment difficult even where mean reversion is intact, with producer prices today and consumer prices tomorrow still ahead. A narrow danger window is published around the 12:30 UTC producer price release and the 13:30 UTC cash open rather than a broad session-wide restriction.
headline: NQ holds 29,471.00 inside an unextended 29,364.00-29,508.25 overnight band with VIX flat at 16.46 and the 10-year easing to 4.84%, while Brent at $101.03 and roughly even odds of a September rate increase keep Stress extreme into the 12:30 UTC producer price release
body:
Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures print 29,471.00, up 22.25 points or 0.08% against a 29,448.75 prior settle, inside an overnight range of 29,364.00 to 29,508.25. That band spans 144.25 points, roughly 0.49%, and is unchanged from the previous hour. The 29,508.25 high was set in the prior hour, rejected immediately, and has not been retested; price now sits about 37 points below it and 107 points above the low. Both extremes of the overnight band have therefore produced retracements, which is mean-reverting behaviour rather than the persistent directional efficiency that defines tail conditions. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 86.15 points or 0.29%, within a 29,334.40 to 29,563.60 range and beneath a 29,507.70 prior close, a third consecutive lower close for the broader Nasdaq Composite.

Cross-asset conditions remain restrictive but have stopped tightening. Brent trades at $101.026, easing 0.18% in what is described as profit-taking while holding above $100 on continued US-Iran escalation and attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. Reuters reporting notes that alternative export routes, non-OPEC supply additions and sharply reduced Chinese seaborne imports have kept the move gradual rather than disorderly, which matters because an orderly oil repricing transmits to equities as a valuation and margin problem rather than as a liquidity shock. The US 10-year yield is 4.84%, down about 0.7 basis points, after reaching roughly 4.85% on 9 September, its highest since late 2023; the 2-year is 4.43%, down about 1.8 basis points. VIX is unchanged at 16.46 with no intraday range, which is a notably contained level given that markets price roughly 60% odds of a 25 basis point increase at the 15-16 September meeting. That combination, high macro stress with contained implied volatility, is the signature of a difficult but two-way environment rather than a pathological one.

Index internals are conflicting on latest-session data. Semiconductors closed broadly higher while seven of eight tracked megacaps closed lower, with cross-sectional dispersion near 2.6 percentage points. Conflicting breadth of this kind reduces directional conviction and raises Stress; it is not evidence of the aligned one-way structure that would justify raising Tail. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run but its collection timestamp is beyond the freshness bound defined by the contract, so it was treated as stale supporting context only and the assessment rests on independently verified current sources.

Scheduled catalysts: August producer prices, core producer prices and weekly jobless claims all release at 12:30 UTC today, with consensus at 0.4% monthly headline, 0.3% core and 205,000 claims. August existing home sales follow at 14:00 UTC against consensus near 3.98 million. August consumer prices release at 12:30 UTC on 11 September. None of these had printed at the assessment cutoff, and no outcome is assumed. Consistent with the risk definition, event importance and forecast dispersion are scored into Stress and Confidence rather than into Tail until an actual price path is observed. Dominant mode is recorded as mixed: range-bound index price action combined with conflicting internals and a restrictive but stable cross-asset backdrop.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 06:00 UTC the mapped policy state was EA_ON in 22 of the 23 available slots, with one WATCH hour at 12:00 UTC on 9 September when Tail reached 20% during a trend-down European session. Tail ranged from 7% to 20% and has held a tight 8-11% band overnight as retracements kept appearing at both ends of the range. Stress climbed from 77% to a sustained 80-83% as Brent broke $100 and the 10-year set fresh highs since late 2023, then settled at 80% for the last three hours. Confidence held between 87% and 89% throughout. The 10:00 UTC slot on 9 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published conditional path keeps Tail in an 11-12% range through the European session, lifts it to 20% in the 12:00 UTC release hour and a horizon peak of 22% in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-release repricing overlaps the US cash open, then decays it to 10-17% across the US afternoon and overnight into the consumer price session. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH; no slot reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in or at the boundary of the extreme band throughout because oil above $100, a 10-year near its highest since late 2023 and roughly even odds of a September rate increase are regime features that a single release does not clear. Confidence decays from 88% to 70% across the horizon as slots move further beyond the observed sample. A narrow danger window is published from 12:25 to 14:00 UTC.
